newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Pacific sells Laidlaw stake.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Pacific sells Laidlaw stake.

text.p: Canadian Pacific Ltd said on Monday it sold all its interest in transportation and waste-management firm Laidlaw Inc in a deal expected to bring in net proceeds of C$1 billion ($722 million).

The Calgary-based conglomerate said it sold nearly 56 million Laidlaw shares, which it will receive after a reclassification of class A and class B voting stock into common shares, expected near the end of July.
The new shares were to be sold in instalments by means of share purchase rights at C$18.85 ($13.61) each, CP said.
Canadian Pacific currently owns 22.5 million, or 47 percent, of Laidlaw's class A shares and 29.7 million, or 11 percent, of its class B non-voting shares.
"We have indicated that Laidlaw, as a portfolio investment, was not a core holding of Canadian Pacific," CP Chairman David O'Brien said in a statement.
CP said it expected to post a gain of C$275 million $199 million) from the sale.
Hamilton, Ontario-based Laidlaw is North America's largest school bus firm and also holds extensive interests in ambulances, health care and waste disposal.
The company has said it expected to produce annualized revenues of $3.6 billion by April 1998.
Its class A shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange closed at C$19.05 and its class B shares at C$18.85 on Monday. The CP announcement was made after the market closed.
Completion of the sale of the rights underlying Laidlaw common shares was subject to the approval by Laidlaw shareholders of the proposed reclassification, CP said.
At a special meeting on July 23, class A shareholders will be asked to okay an exchange of 1.15 common shares for each class A share. Class B shareholders will be asked to approve a one-for-one swap.
